stem: If \(\dfrac{1}{\sin^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\cos^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\tan^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\cot^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\sec^2\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta} = -3\), then find the value of \(\theta\).
solution: Rewrite each reciprocal: the expression becomes \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \sec^2\theta - \cot^2\theta - \tan^2\theta - \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta\). Group as \((\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta) - (\sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta) - (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)\). Using \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1\) and \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\): \(1 - (\sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta) - 1 = -3\), so \(\sec^2\theta + \tan^2\theta = 3\). Since \(\sec^2\theta = 1 + \tan^2\theta\): \(1 + 2\tan^2\theta = 3 \Rightarrow \tan^2\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \tan\theta = 1\). \(\therefore \theta = 45^\circ\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: A cylinder of radius 12 cm contains water up to a height of 20 cm. A spherical iron ball is dropped into the cylinder and the water level rises by 6.75 cm. What is the radius of the iron ball?
solution: Volume of water displaced (rise) equals the volume of the sphere. \(\pi r_{\text{cyl}}^2 h = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). \(\therefore 12^2 \times 6.75 = \dfrac{4}{3} r^3\). \(144 \times 6.75 = 972 = \dfrac{4}{3} r^3\). \(\therefore r^3 = \dfrac{972 \times 3}{4} = 729\). \(\therefore r = 9\) cm. The radius of the iron ball is 9 cm.

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Draw a circle with centre O and radius 3 cm. Draw tangent segments PA and PB through a point P outside the circle such that \(\angle APB = 70^\circ\).
solution: Since PA and PB are tangents, \(OA \perp PA\) and \(OB \perp PB\), so \(\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ\). In quadrilateral OAPB, \(\angle AOB = 360^\circ - 90^\circ - 90^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ\). Construction steps: (1) Draw a circle with centre O and radius 3 cm. (2) Draw two radii OA and OB such that \(\angle AOB = 110^\circ\). (3) At A draw a ray perpendicular to OA, and at B draw a ray perpendicular to OB. (4) The two perpendicular rays meet at point P. Then PA and PB are the required tangent segments, and \(\angle APB = 70^\circ\).
